attempted_claim: On the rectangle Omega=(-1,1)x(0,1) consider the critical Grushin system dt f - dx^2 f - x^2 dy^2 f = 0 with homogeneous Dirichlet conditions, controlled only by Dirichlet data u(t,x) on the single transverse side Gamma=(-1,1)x{y=1} (the side orthogonal to the degeneracy line {x=0}, zero Dirichlet elsewhere) and L^2 initial data. Decide exactly which of the three alternatives holds: (a) null-controllable from Gamma for every T>0, or (b) null-controllable from Gamma if and only if T>T* for some finite sharp T*>0 to be determined exactly, or (c) never null-controllable from Gamma for any T>0. A complete answer establishes the correct alternative with full proof, including a boundary observability inequality when controllability is claimed and an explicit normalized adjoint sequence falsifying uniform boundary observability whenever non-controllability below a time or for all times is claimed.
decisive_failure: Single-mode computations reach only m=1..8 and the packet Gramian probe is truncated at 8x8, so neither yields uniformity in the frequency parameter mu=m*pi; the uniform biorthogonal/Riesz and mu-uniform Carleman bounds needed to separate always vs threshold vs never remain unproved, and no emergent finding is claimed.
